stem: In a first order reaction, the concentration of reactant decreases from \(20\ \mathrm{mmol\ dm^{-3}}\) to \(8\ \mathrm{mmol\ dm^{-3}}\) in \(38\) minutes. What is the half life of reaction?
The half life of a first order reaction is \(1.7\) hours. How long will it take for \(20\%\) of the reactant to react?

The energy of activation for a first order reaction is \(104\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}\). The rate constant at \(25\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}\) is \(3.7 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}\). What is the rate constant at \(30\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}\)? \((R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J/K\ mol})\)
What is the energy of activation of a reaction whose rate constant doubles when the temperature changes from \(303\ \mathrm{K}\) to \(313\ \mathrm{K}\)?

The rate constant of a reaction at \(500\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}\) is \(1.6 \times 10^{3}\ \mathrm{M^{-1}s^{-1}}\). What is the frequency factor of the reaction if its activation energy is \(56\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}\).
Show that time required for \(99.9\%\) completion of a first order reaction is three times the time required for \(90\%\) completion.
A first order reaction takes \(40\) minutes for \(30\%\) decomposition. Calculate its half life.
The rate constant for the first order reaction is given by \(\log_{10} k = 14.34 - 1.25 \times 10^{4}\ T\). Calculate activation energy of the reaction.
What fraction of molecules in a gas at \(300\ \mathrm{K}\) collide with an energy equal to activation energy of \(50\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}\) ?
